$comment: P68 round 12 (lane `cs`, D-C-AN-ENUMERATED-TYPE-IS-NOT-COMPATIBLE-WITH-ITS-UNDERLYING-INTEGER-TYPE): the integer type an enumerated type is compatible with (C 6.7.2.2p4, C23 6.7.3.3p13, p16) under the SysV / AAPCS / Darwin convention the ELF and Mach-O formats declare (`enumCompatibleTypeRule: "gnu"`): `unsigned int` when no value is negative, `int` otherwise, the declared type for a fixed underlying type — and every place it is observable: `_Generic` (a pointer to the enumeration too), silent pointer conversions, redeclarations spelling either type, the enumeration's arithmetic (`e - 1` for `e == 0` stored in a `long` is 4294967295) and its bit-fields' signedness. Targets: only the formats that declare this convention, all LP64 (pe64 declares `msvc`: see enum_compatible_type_msvc_rule). MEASURED 2026-09-24, this file compiled and RUN on each reference separately at -std=c2x: gcc 13.3.0 and clang 18.1.3 on x86_64, and aarch64-linux-gnu-gcc 13.3.0 and clang 18.1.3 --target=aarch64-linux-gnu under qemu-aarch64, and Apple clang 21.0.0 (arm64-apple-darwin25.6.0) on the Mac, exit 42 (gcc -Wall warns -Wenum-int-mismatch on the redeclarations); mingw-w64 13.2.0, which follows the same rule on LLP64, runs every check but the `long` one (its 32-bit `long` wraps 4294967295 to -1; its `long long` holds 4294967295); the -std=c17 -pedantic-errors modes and MSVC 19.51 refuse the C23 `: long` clause. Before this round DSS selected `default`, warned on the pointer conversions, refused all four redeclarations, and gave the non-negative enumeration `int` arithmetic (its bit-field read -1, and `e - 1` stored -1 where gcc and clang store 4294967295). exit 42 = every check holds.
